exposure: level of training (obstetrics and gynecology residents vs. attending physicians)
reported reasons for not counseling (lack of time, lack of sufficient information)
outcome: prenatal counseling practices related to postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction (urinary incontinence, fecal incontinence)
cohort: Obstetrical providers at centers with integrated urogynecology services.
finding: Prenatal counseling regarding pelvic floor dysfunction risk is largely lacking among obstetrical providers at all levels of training, with residents significantly less likely to discuss these topics than attending physicians.
cross-section timing: The survey assessed current prenatal counseling practices.
